title: अविद्या/माया चिन्तनका दृष्टिमा ऋतुविचार खण्डकाव्य (Rituvichara Khandakavya in view of Avidya/Maya Thoughts)
nepali: ऋतुविचार खण्डकाव्यलाई पौरस्त्य दर्शनको अविद्या÷मायासम्बन्धी मान्यताका आधारमा विवेचना गरिएको यस अनुसन्धानात्मक लेखका निम्ति आवश्यक सामग्री पुस्तकालयीय स्रोतबाट सङ्कलन गरिएको छ र सैद्धान्तिक आधारको निर्माणमा निगमनात्मक विधिको प्रयोग गरिएको छ । यस क्रममा क्रमशः उपनिषद्, साङ्ख्य, योग, न्याय, वैशेषिक, मीमांसा, वेदान्त र बौद्ध दर्शनका अविद्यासम्बन्धी स्थापनाहरूको अनुशीलन र ऋतुविचार खण्डकाव्यको सूक्ष्मपठन गरी अविद्यासम्बन्धी चिन्तन अभिव्यञ्जित प्रमुख श्लोकहरू ठम्याएर तिनीहरूको व्याख्या÷विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । अन्त्यमा ऋतुविचार खण्डकाव्यको मूल अलङ्कार्य विषय परिवर्तनमूलक ऋतुचव्रmसम्बन्धी प्रकृतिचित्रण रहे पनि अध्यात्मसम्बन्धी विषयगत विम्बहरू प्रकृतिचित्रणका सन्दर्भमा नै आएका छन् । यसरी काव्यमा अध्यात्मसम्बन्धी विषयगत विम्बहरूले पनि प्राकृतिक परिवर्तनमूलक ऋतुचव्रmसम्बन्धी मूल विषयवस्तुभित्र नै स्थान पाएका छन् र पौरस्त्य दर्शनको अविद्या÷मायासम्बन्धी चिन्तन पनि अलङ्कार्यका रूपमा नभएर अलङ्कारका रूपमा व्यक्त भएको छ । यस खण्डकाव्यमा व्यक्त अविद्या÷मायाचिन्तनमा साङ्ख्य, योग, न्याय, वैशेषिक, मीमांसा र वेदान्तको प्रभाव लेखनाथको अध्ययन एवं श्रवण, मनन तथा निदिध्यासनगत भए तापनि बौद्ध दर्शनको प्रभाव भने उपर्युक्त दर्शनहरूसँग बौद्ध दर्शनको साम्यता र कविको पूर्वसंस्कारगत हो भन्ने निष्कर्ष दिइएको छ । (Rituvichara Khandakavya has been analyzed on the basis of Paurastya Darshan's notions of ignorance(avidya) and love (maya) in this article. The necessary material for this research article has been collected from library sources and deductive method has been used in the construction of the theoretical base. In this sequence, the Upanishad, Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta and Buddhist philosophy related to Avidya were studied and Rituvichara Khandakavya was carefully read and the main verses expressing thoughts on Avidya were identified and analyzed. In the end, although the main decorative theme of Rituvichar Khandakavya is nature depiction related to changing seasons, the thematic symbols related to spirituality have come in the context of nature depiction. In this way, the thematic symbols related to spirituality in the poetry have also found a place within the main theme related to the natural changing seasons, and the thought about ignorance and love in Paurastya philosophy has also been expressed not as a cause to figure of speech but as a figure of speech. Although the influence of Sankhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa and Vedanta in Avidya/Maya thinking expressed in this ode poem is consistent with Lekhnath's study and hearing, meditation and Nididhya; it has been concluded that the influence of Buddhist philosophy is the closeness of Buddhist philosophy with the above-mentioned philosophies, and earlier-cultural concept of the poet.)
american_english: For this analytical article, which examines the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’ on the basis of the Eastern philosophical concepts of ignorance (avidya) and illusion (maya), the necessary materials were collected from library sources, and a deductive method was used in constructing the theoretical foundation. In this process, the positions on ignorance in the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta, and Buddhist philosophies were studied in sequence, and through a close reading of the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’, the principal verses expressing thoughts related to ignorance were identified and their explanation and analysis were carried out. Finally, although the main figurative subject of the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’ is the depiction of nature related to the transformative cycle of the seasons, the thematic images related to spirituality have appeared within the context of that depiction of nature. In this way, the thematic images related to spirituality in the poem have also found their place within the main subject matter related to the transformative cycle of the seasons, and the Eastern philosophical thought concerning ignorance and illusion has been expressed not as the figurative subject but as a figure of expression. Although Lekhnath’s study and his practices of listening, contemplation, and meditation show the influence of Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta in the thought of ignorance and illusion expressed in this khandakavya, it is concluded that the influence of Buddhist philosophy is due to its similarity with the aforementioned philosophies and to the poet’s prior dispositions.

informal_english: This analytical article looks at the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’ through the Eastern philosophical ideas of ignorance (avidya) and illusion (maya), and the necessary material for it was collected from library sources, with a deductive method used to build the theoretical base. In the process, the views on ignorance in the Upanishads, Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, Vedanta, and Buddhist philosophies were studied one by one, and by doing a close reading of the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’, the main verses that express thoughts about ignorance were picked out and then explained and analysed. In the end, even though the main figurative focus of the khandakavya ‘Rituvichar’ is the depiction of nature linked to the changing cycle of the seasons, the thematic images related to spirituality pop up within that same context of nature depiction. So, the spiritual thematic images in the poem also find their place inside the main subject matter of the transformative seasonal cycle, and the Eastern philosophical thinking about ignorance and illusion comes through not as the figurative subject but as a figure of expression. Even though Lekhnath’s study and his practices of listening, contemplation, and meditation show the influence of Samkhya, Yoga, Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Mimamsa, and Vedanta in the way ignorance and illusion are thought about in this khandakavya, the article concludes that the influence of Buddhist philosophy comes from its similarity to those philosophies and from the poet’s prior dispositions.
